blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Web text makes up the majority of pretraining data and is increasingly AI-generated. After applying FineWeb quality filtering, we find that 27.5% of tokens from June 2026 web data are labeled as AI-generated by Pangram, rising to 31.1% by August. Unlike synthetic data or model-collapse setups, this wild AI text comes from many models, is written for human readers, and arrives unlabeled in pretraining corpora.
How does AI text in the wild affect language model pretraining?
To answer this question, we pretrain 800 language models (19.9M to 973M parameters), varying the ratio of added AI tokens to human tokens, and fit scaling laws to held-out losses on both human and AI-generated text. For data-starved models, adding AI tokens to pretraining data initially lowers loss on human text, but the benefit saturates as more are added and quickly reverses into harm. For models trained on high budgets of human text, AI tokens raise loss almost immediately, while the same number of fresh human tokens keeps lowering it. Existing scaling laws such as
Chinchilla ( Hoffmann et al., 2022 ) ,
which treat AI tokens as no different from human tokens, fail to predict this behavior. We propose a new scaling law with separate benefit and harm terms that allows the value of an AI token (measured in human token equivalents) to change sign while also reducing to Chinchilla in the absence of AI text. When fit on smaller models, our scaling law predicts the effect of AI text on held-out human-text loss for models up to 3.6 × \times larger with 41% lower error than the best existing law over all AI ratios. It implies that training on unfiltered
web text at August 2026’s AI share (31.1%) requires 1.6 × \times as much compute as training on its human subset at 20 tokens per parameter, a gap that grows with the human budget.
We recommend filtering AI text when the target is human text, repeating human text before expanding the training dataset with AI-generated web text, and reporting validation loss on human and AI text separately, since at a 22.3% AI share (our 2026 evaluation crawl), mixed validation sets hide the harm in 95.5% of harmful runs. AI text remains valuable when the target is AI text.
We release Wild AI , an 83B-token corpus with AI, topic, and format labels, all 800 models and code at https://github.com/pangramlabs/WildAI .

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
AI-generated text is flooding the web.
In the June 2026 Common Crawl, Pangram labels 27.5% of the tokens
that pass FineWeb’s quality filters as AI-generated, up from 10.1% two years earlier and rising to 31.1% in August 2026 ( Figure 1 ). At the same time, models are trained far past the compute-optimal budget of ∼ \sim 20 tokens per parameter ( Hoffmann et al., 2022 ) ; for example, Qwen3-32B is trained on ∼ \sim 1,100 tokens per parameter ( Yang et al., 2025 ) . Models are also projected to exhaust nearly all public human-written text by 2032 ( Villalobos et al., 2024 ) . Every new crawl thus forces a choice about what to do with the AI-generated documents: keep them, filter them, or find some optimal data mixture of AI and human text.

AI生成的文本淹没了网络.
在2026年6月的"普通爬行"中,Pangram标签为27.5%的代币.
超过FineWeb质量过滤器为AI生成, 与此同时,模型的培训远超过计算-最佳预算的\\sim 20个每个参数的符号(Hoffmann等人,2022年);例如,Qune3-32B的培训是\sim 1,100个参数的符号(Yang等人,2025年)。 据预测,模型到2032年还将耗尽几乎所有公开的人文文字(Villalobos等人,2024年)。 每个新的爬行都迫使人们对AI生成的文档做出选择:保留它们,过滤它们,或者找到AI和人类文本的最佳数据混合物.

blocks.en:
In this paper, we measure how AI-generated web text affects pretraining and fit scaling laws that predict its impact. No previous work directly addresses this question: model-collapse studies train a model recursively on its own output ( Shumailov et al., 2024 ; Gerstgrasser et al., 2024 ) , and synthetic-data studies add curated rephrasings designed to help performance in specific domains ( Maini et al., 2024 ; Kang et al., 2025 ) .
We study a third kind, which we call wild AI text: text that language models wrote for human readers and that occurs naturally on the web, rather than being generated for training. It comes from many models, arrives in pretraining corpora unlabeled and mixed with human text, varies in quality, and makes up a rising share of the web.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们衡量AI生成的网络文本如何影响预训和适应预测其影响的缩放法. 以往没有一项工作直接涉及这个问题:模型-缩合研究对模型进行自输出递归式的训练(Shumailov等人,2024年;Gerstgrasser等人,2024年),合成数据研究增加了旨在帮助特定领域业绩的编译重写(Maini等人,2024年;Kang等人,2025年)。
我们研究的是第三种,我们称之为野性的AI文本:语言模型为人类读者写的文本,这些文本在网络上自然出现,而不是为培训而生成的. 它来自许多型号,到达前训练的未加标签且与人类文字混合,质量各异,并构成网络份额不断上升.

blocks.en:
We pretrain 800 models (19.9M to 973M parameters), adding up to 64 wild AI tokens per human token to fixed human corpora, and evaluate them on held-out human text (C4, FineWeb, and Paloma) as well as on AI text. AI text helps only data-starved models: it lowers loss on human text below about 10 human tokens per parameter, but from the Chinchilla-optimal 20 its benefit disappears, and larger amounts of AI tokens raise loss, while the same number of fresh human tokens still lowers it.
Existing laws either treat AI tokens as human ones (Chinchilla), never let their value fall below zero (most repetition laws), or fit harm without separating it from benefit (most mixture laws). To address this, we propose a scaling law for wild AI-generated text
that pairs a saturating benefit with a harm penalty that grows logarithmically and that reduces to Chinchilla without AI text. Fit on models up to 268M, it predicts models 3.6 × \times larger with a paired error (the RMSE of the predicted change in log loss against each run’s human-only control) of 0.83 × 10 − 3 0.83\times 10^{-3} on C4, against 1.41 × 10 − 3 1.41\times 10^{-3} for the best existing law ( Shukor et al., 2025 ) and 4.32 × 10 − 3 4.32\times 10^{-3} for Chinchilla ( Hoffmann et al., 2022 ) .

blocks.en: Using our new law, we propose concrete recommendations for dealing with the rising share of wild AI text. Training on unfiltered web text at August 2026’s AI share (31.1%) takes 1.6 × \times the compute of training on its human subset, rising to 3.0 × \times by 2028 at the forecast AI share, and repeating human text beats adding AI text. Current quality filters make this worse by favoring AI text. FineWeb’s pipeline ( Penedo et al., 2024a ) keeps AI documents 2.3 × \times as often as human ones, and the DCLM pipeline ( Li et al., 2024 ) keeps AI documents 9.8 × \times as often. AI text is easier to predict, so a validation set with a 22.3% AI share (our 2026 evaluation crawl) hides the harm in 95.5% of harmful runs. For predicting AI text itself (Cosmopedia) the optimal training mix is over 90% AI. We release Wild AI , our 96M-document dataset with AI, topic, and format labels, and all 800 models. 1 1 1 Data and code at https://github.com/pangramlabs/WildAI

blocks.en: 2 Measuring AI-Generated Web Data
blocks.zh: 2 测量AI-Gened Web数据

blocks.en: In this section, we describe how we create a large-scale dataset of web data, broken down into human-written and AI-generated corpora. We find that 27.5% of June 2026 tokens that pass the FineWeb filters are AI-generated, a share that is rising each month, that the AI share is uneven across topics and formats, and that existing pretraining quality filters (FineWeb and DCLM) favor it.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们描述了我们如何创建一个网络数据的大规模数据集,细分为人文和AI生成的corpora. 我们发现,2026年6月27.5%的通过FineWeb过滤器的标语是AI生成的,这个比例逐月上升,AI共享在话题和格式上不均匀,现有的预训质量过滤器(FineWeb和DCLM)也赞成.

blocks.en: We use the FineWeb corpus ( Penedo et al., 2024a ) , a subset of Common Crawl ( Common Crawl Foundation, 2007 ) . We extend past the June 2025 cutoff point by replicating the FineWeb filtering process on Common Crawl data from July 2025 to June 2026. 2 2 2 We use FineWeb v1.4.0; more details are in § A . We collect a dataset of 96.04M documents (83.31B tokens), which we call Wild AI .
blocks.zh: 我们使用FineWebacle(Penedo等人,2024a),这是Common Crawl(Common Crawl Foundation,2007)的一个子集. 我们在2025年7月至2026年6月期间复制了FineWeb在Common Crawl数据上的过滤程序,从而延长了2025年6月的截止点。 2 2 我们使用 FineWeb v1.4.0;详见§A. 我们收集96.04M文件(83.31B令牌)的数据集,我们称之为Wild AI。

blocks.en: To understand the provenance of our data, we label each text as AI-generated or human-written. We first run EditLens Llama-3.2-3B ( Thai et al., 2026 ) to label vast quantities of text (more than 280B tokens, from which we draw the 83B tokens of Wild AI ). We then run the more accurate Pangram 3.3.2 on documents confidently labeled AI-generated and human-written as a second check, using those labels to create our final human-written corpus of 58.91M documents (42.19B tokens) and AI-generated corpus of 32.54M documents (35.32B tokens). 3 3 3 Because EditLens preselects likely AI documents, AI text is 42% of Wild AI ’s tokens, far more than on the web. Wild AI is a pool for building training mixtures, not a natural sample of the web (§ A ). Pangram 3.3.2 has a reported false-positive rate of 0.05% and false-negative rate of 1.99% ( Glickenhaus et al., 2026 ) , accurate enough at this scale to separate the AI and human distributions. On pre-ChatGPT web text, Pangram 3.3.2 labels 0.062% of 60,000 documents from 2021 crawls AI. 4 4 4 An upper bound on the FPR, since pre-2022 web text may itself contain some AI-generated text. We use WebOrganizer ( Wettig et al., 2025 ) to extract topic and format labels per document.

blocks.en:
To assess the increase in AI content on the web, we run Pangram on a sample of 310,000 documents, dated from January 2021 through August 2026. 5 5 5 5,000 documents for each month that has an associated Common Crawl. In June of 2021, less than 0.1% of FineWeb tokens were AI-generated. By June 2024, it was 10.1%, 16.1% in June 2025, and 27.5% in June 2026 (see Figure 1 , left, and Figure 8 ). The rise continues: in August 2026 the share was 31.1%, 3.6 points above June (§ A.2 ). Moreover, there is a large distribution mismatch between human-written and AI-generated content that continues to grow ( He et al., 2026 ) . In Figure 2 , tutorials are 6.2% of human-labeled tokens and 18.5% of AI-labeled tokens, and personal blogs 8.6 and 1.0% (see Figure 7 ).
Increasingly, the formats and topics of web data will reflect LLM outputs rather than human writing. We hypothesize that this may lead models to stray further from the human distribution on topics AI rarely writes about.

网络数据的格式和专题将越来越多地反映LLM产出,而不是人类写作。 我们假设这可能导致模型在AI很少写的主题上进一步偏离人类分布.

blocks.en: To understand the effects of different quality filtering processes, we audit a subset of 10,000 raw Common Crawl documents and track which portion of human- and AI-written texts make it through each step of the filtration process ( Figure 2 , see § A.1 ). We examine both FineWeb ( Penedo et al., 2024a ) and DCLM ( Li et al., 2024 ) filtering processes, finding that AI-generated texts pass FineWeb’s pipeline 2.3 × \times (29.3% vs. 12.8%) and DCLM’s full pipeline 9.8 × \times (14.5% vs. 1.5%) as often as human-written documents. These filters are insufficient at filtering out AI-generated text, and in fact heavily prefer it.

blocks.en: In Chinchilla, the data term ( B B / D β D^{\beta} ) depends only on the total token count D D , without accounting for differences between unique tokens and repeated ones. To address this, Muennighoff et al. (2023) extended Chinchilla to account for repeated data by allowing for the effective value of a repeated token to be lower than a new unique token, but never below zero. Qin et al. (2026) propose that the effective value of a token relies not only on unique tokens but also on model size. Lovelace et al. (2026) alternatively propose that repetition is best modeled not by effective data but by adding an overfitting penalty.

blocks.en: Other scaling laws model pretraining data from many domains or languages. Shumailov et al. (2024) study degradation under recursive training on model-generated data. Subsequent work examines how retaining original data or generating synthetic data from each successive model generation changes this behavior ( Gerstgrasser et al., 2024 ; Seddik et al., 2024 ) , and how collapse rates depend on the recursive estimation setting ( Suresh et al., 2024 ) . Schaeffer et al. (2025) show that loss increases, divergent error, and loss of distributional tails
are distinct outcomes, while Dohmatob et al. (2024) ; Dohmatob et al. (2025) show that synthetic data can affect scaling behavior even in the non-recursive setting. Kang et al. (2025) find that the benefits of synthetic rephrasings and textbooks mixed with web text depend on budget. Similarly, Zhu et al. (2025) show worsened performance on Paloma as synthetic text replaces natural text at a fixed token budget. Kazdan et al. (2025) show that the benefit of synthetic data depends on total data budget.

blocks.en: 4 Scaling Laws for Human-Written and AI-Generated Text
blocks.zh: 4 增强人文文字和人工智能文本的法律

blocks.en: Models trained on only human text follow Chinchilla scaling laws, but when trained on a portion of AI-generated text, AI tokens initially help models with low budgets of human text but harm models with high budgets. We create five criteria for a scaling law to model this phenomenon, and propose our scaling law that fits these criteria. Our law has the lowest error predicting the effects of adding AI-generated text versus existing scaling laws (0.83 vs. the second best of 1.41 × 10 − 3 \times 10^{-3} on C4).
blocks.zh: 仅接受人文文本培训的模型遵循钦奇拉缩放法,但在接受部分AI生成文本培训时,AI符号最初帮助人文文本预算低但损害高预算模型的模型. 我们制定了五项标准来制定规模法以模拟这种现象,并提出了符合这些标准的规模法。 我们的法律在预测增加AI生成的文本与现有的缩放定律(0.83 vs. second best of 1.41 × 10 − 3\times 10^{-3} on C4)的效果时,有最小的误差.

blocks.en: We train 800 models of varying sizes, human tokens per parameter ( T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} ), and ratios of AI to human data r r . We find that Chinchilla scaling laws are inadequate at predicting the behavior of AI-generated text and propose a new scaling law that models both the benefits and harms of pretraining on AI-generated web text.

blocks.en: We train 800 models varying in size from 19.9M to 973M, with 2.9 to 87.5 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} , and r r of 0 to 64. We use the nanochat architecture due to its fast training and high performance relative to model size ( Karpathy, 2025 ) . 6 6 6 See § B for the architecture, training setup, and how N N is counted, following Pearce and Song (2024) . We evaluate on human-, mixed-, and AI-generated text sets. We use C4 ( Raffel et al., 2020 ) as our north star dataset to model human text, similar to the frontier Marin model evaluation ( Marin Community, 2025 ) . We also evaluate on Paloma ( Magnusson et al., 2024 ) , reporting the loss macro-averaged over its 16 sources, and a held-out set of pre-2022 FineWeb data (FW22). For mixed text, we evaluate on a held-out set of 2026 FineWeb data (FW26), which contains 22.3% AI-generated text. We also evaluate both the AI- and human-written splits of FineWeb 2026 (FW26-AI and FW26-H, respectively). To observe effects on purely AI text, we evaluate on Cosmopedia ( Ben Allal et al., 2024 , Cosmo) . Human text is our main target. It is the language a pretrained model is meant to model, and loss on held-out text is a standard proxy for downstream performance ( Huang et al., 2024 ; Gadre et al., 2025 ) .

We find that for models where we add more human tokens, Chinchilla scaling laws perform as expected, but adapt poorly to predicting how models with AI-generated tokens will behave.
On the reserved sizes, Chinchilla predicts the fresh-human additions to a paired error of 1.32 × 10 − 3 1.32\times 10^{-3} on C4 but the AI additions only to 4.32 × 10 − 3 4.32\times 10^{-3} . blocks.en: We fit our scaling law on 726 models of 19.9M to 268M parameters, and evaluate our fit on 74 models of 477M and 973M parameters, 1.8 × 1.8\times and 3.6 × 3.6\times the largest fitted size ( Table 5 ). We benchmark existing scaling laws developed for repetition, data mixing, and surrogate data in Table 1 . 10 10 10 § C.3 defines the laws; § E has full results. Our law has the lowest paired error across all four human sources (0.83 × 10 − 3 \times 10^{-3} on C4). 11 11 11 On human text our law’s lead over the best existing law is statistically significant over all AI ratios (§ E.1 ). Shukor et al. ’s joint law ( Equation 11 ), which treats AI and human text as two separate data mixtures, is the best of the existing laws on human text (1.41 × 10 − 3 \times 10^{-3} on C4) and is the best of all laws when the target text is AI-generated. 12 12 12 Results on mixed and AI-generated target texts are in Table 9 .
blocks.zh: 我们的缩放定律适用于726种19.9M到268M参数的模型,并评价我们是否适合74种477M和973M参数的模型,1.8×1.8乘和3.6×3.6乘最大尺寸的模型(表5)。 我们在表110 10 10 § C.3中将为重复、数据混合和替代数据而制定的现有比例法作为基准,界定了法律;§E有全部结果。 我们的法律在所有四个人类来源(0.83×10 – 3\times 10^{-3})上都存在最小的对等误差, Shukor等人的联合法(第11条方程式)将AI和人类文本作为两个独立的数据混合物处理,是现存关于人类文本的法律中最好的(1.41 × 10 − 3\times 10^{-3}在C4上),当目标文本是AI生成时是所有法律中最好的. 12 关于混合文本和人工智能生成的目标文本的结果见表9。

blocks.en: 5 The Effects of Training on AI Text and What to Do About It
blocks.zh: 5 培训对大赦国际文本的影响和对此应做些什么

blocks.en:
We forecast that over half (50.7%) of FineWeb tokens will be AI-generated by the end of 2028. An unfiltered crawl at August 2026’s AI share (31.1%) needs 1.6 × \times the compute,
and 3.0 × \times in 2028, to match a filtered model at 20 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} . blocks.en: 5.1 The Cost of Not Filtering
blocks.zh: 5.1 不过滤的成本

Left: change in loss from removing the AI documents of a 22.3% AI mix without replacing them, predicted by our law (color; black line: no change) and measured (circles; values for 973M). blocks.en: Mohri et al. (2026) find that with sufficient compute, it is best to not filter data at all for pretraining. To test this for AI-generated text, we train models at the 2026 natural rate of AI (22.3%), and paired models of the same size with only the human subset of pretraining data. Despite having less data, models above about 10 to 15 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} (less at larger sizes) had lower loss on C4, as shown in Figure 5 . Our law gets the direction of filtering right in 18 of the 19 pairs (paired error 3.28 × 10 − 3 3.28\times 10^{-3} ), while Chinchilla predicts that removing the AI text raises loss in all 13 pairs where it lowers it. We also find that the more human-written tokens a model has, the larger the benefit in loss reduction is. As most models today are trained far past 20 tokens per parameter, we recommend removing all AI-generated web text for human next-token prediction.
blocks.zh: Mohri等人(2026年)发现,只要有足够的计算,最好完全不过滤数据进行预训. 为了测试AI生成的文本,我们以AI的2026自然速率(22.3%)来训练模型,并且只用人类子集的预训数据来配对大小相同的模型. 尽管数据较少,但如图5所示,高于10至15T P P h TPP_{h}(体积较小)的模型C4损失较低。 我们的定律在19对中的18对中获得了过滤正确的方向(paired error 3.28 × 10 − 3 3.28\times 10^{-3}),而钦奇拉预测删除AI文本会在它降低时引起所有13对文本的损失. 我们还发现,一个模型所写的人文符号越多,减少损失的好处就越大。 由于今天大多数的模型都训练了 远超过每个参数的20个符号, 我们建议删除所有人工智能生成的网络文本, 用于人类的下一个预测。

blocks.en:
Using our historical sample of 5,000 documents per month, we use a random walk with drift ( Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, 2021 ) to forecast the future proportion of AI tokens. 13 13 13 More details about our forecasting methodology and predictions are in § A.2 . Extrapolating the average monthly rise, it forecasts 42.3% AI tokens by the end of 2027 and 50.7% by the end of 2028.
Compute-equivalent gain (CEG) ( Davidson et al., 2023 ) compares the compute efficiency of any two models. Using a model trained with 22.3% AI (the AI share of our 2026 crawl) as our reference model, our law predicts that the reference (an unfiltered model) needs 1.3 × \times the compute to match human-only training at 268M parameters and 20 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} ( Equation 17 ). At August 2026’s AI share (31.1%) it needs 1.6 × \times . At the forecast AI share, by the end of 2027 a model will need 2.1 × \times the compute to match a filtered model’s performance on C4, and 3.0 × \times by the end of 2028 ( Figure 1 ).
blocks.zh:
利用我们每月5000份文件的历史样本,我们用漂移的随机行走(Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, 2021)来预测AI符的未来比例. 13 13 更多关于我们的预测方法和预测的细节载于§A.2. 推算月均上涨,预测2027年底为42.3%,2028年底为50.7%。
计算等效增益(CEG)(Davidson等人,2023年)比较任意两种模型的计算效率. 以22.3%AI(我们2026年爬行的AI份额)作为我们的参考模型,我们的法律预测,参考(未过滤模型)需要1.3x\x计算,以268M参数和20 TP h TPP_{h}(方程式17)来匹配人类唯一的训练。 2026年8月的AI份额(31.1%)需要1.6xxxxxx时间。 在预测的AI共享中,到2027年底,一个模型需要2.1××的计算时间来匹配一个过滤模型在C4上的性能,到2028年底时需要3.0×××的计算时间(图1).

blocks.en: Muennighoff et al. (2023) and Qin et al. (2026) model repeated tokens as effective tokens, and Lovelace et al. (2026) with an overfitting penalty. To compare the effects of repeating human tokens and adding AI tokens, we train 19.9M and 35.8M models at 20 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} that add 1, 4, or 8 times the human corpus in tokens, either by repeating it or by adding AI text. For C4, loss after one added epoch was 2.3% lower when repeating human tokens than when adding fresh AI tokens, a gap that expands to 6.3--6.4% after eight added epochs (nine in total). 14 14 14 See § F.3 for experimental setup details and additional results.
blocks.zh: Muennighoff等人(2023年)和秦等人(2026年)的模型重复代币作为有效代币,而Lovelace等人(2026年)则受到过重的处罚. 为了比较重复人类标志物和添加AI标志物的效果,我们在20 T P P h TPP_{h)时训练了19.9M和35.8M型号,通过重复或添加AI文本,将人类标志物加到1,4或8倍. 就C4而言,一个增加的时代之后,重复人类标志时的损失比增加新的AI标志时低2.3%,这一差距在八个增加的时代(总共9个)之后扩大至6.3-6.4%。 14 14 实验设置细节和额外结果见§F.3。

blocks.en: 5.2 When Is AI Text Worth Training On?
blocks.zh: 5.2 当AI文本值得培训时?

blocks.en: When predicting on human text, AI text helps only when human training data is scarce: the loss-minimizing AI share on C4 is 37% at 5 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} but 1.0% by 20 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} , and FW22 and Paloma behave similarly ( Figure 6 , § F.2 ). On AI-generated text, the optimal share stays above 90% at every budget, and our law values the first AI token at more than 20 human tokens ( η \eta in Table 7 ).
blocks.zh: 在预测人类文字时,AI文本只有在人类训练数据稀缺时才会有所帮助:C4上的损失最小化AI份额为37%,在5 T P P h TPP_{h},但到20 T P P h TPP_{h}时为1.0%,FW22和Paloma行为相似(图6,§F.2). 在人工智能生成的文本中,每个预算的最佳份额保持在90%以上,我们的法律在20多个人类符号中评价第一个人工智能标志(\\\eta,表7)。

blocks.en: In agentic workflows, models increasingly prompt other models and read their outputs, so a model must understand AI-written input as well as human input. Understanding such text need not mean writing it, yet training on AI text changes how a model writes: at 268M, AI-typical phrases per 1,000 words rise from 0.16 without AI text to 0.36 at r = 1 r=1 and 0.54 at r = 4 r=4 , and at r = 2 r=2 Pangram labels twice as many stories AI (37.2% vs. 18.6%, Table 13 ). 15 15 15 See § G for details on AI-typical phrases and Pangram labeling.
blocks.zh: 在代理工作流程中,模型越来越多地激发其他模型并读取其输出,因此一个模型必须理解AI-书面输入以及人类输入. 理解这种文字不一定意味着写作,但AI文字的培训改变了模型的写作方式:在268M时,AI-典型的词组每千字从没有AI文字的0.16升到0.36,在r=1r=1,在r=4r=4时0.54,在r=2r=2时. Pangram的标签是AI的两倍(37.2%对18.6%,表13). 15 15 关于AI-典型短语和Pangram标签的细节参见§G.

blocks.en: Mixture laws that model the two as separate domains, such as the joint law of Shukor et al. (2025) , are the most accurate existing laws in our benchmark, and the split could go further, since AI and human web text differ in format (tutorials are 18.5% of AI-labeled tokens but 6.2% of human-labeled ones). Because AI text is easier to predict, all 553 models with added AI text lower loss on AI-labeled FW26 text, while raising loss on human-labeled text in 44% of models. At our 2026 crawl’s 22.3% AI share, a mixed validation set reports 95.5% of these harmful runs as improvements ( Figure 6 ). Tuned against C4, our law recommends 1.0% AI at 20 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} , and tuned against FW26, 56% but only 2.0% on the human subset. We recommend reporting loss on human and AI text separately.
blocks.zh: 将两者作为单独领域的混合法,例如Shukor等人(2025年)的联合法,是我们基准中最准确的现行法律,这种分割可能更进一步,因为AI和人类网络文本在格式上有所不同(教义是AI标签的18.5%,而人类标签的6.2%)。 由于AI文本比较容易预测,所有添加AI文本的553模型都降低了AI标签的FW26文本的损失,同时在44%的模型中提高了人类标签文本的损失. 在2026年的Graw22.3%的AI份额上, 校对:Soup 我们建议分别报告人文和人工智能文本的损失。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: Wild AI text now makes up over a quarter of filtered web crawls, and its share is rising. Across 800 pretrained models, it helps only data-starved models, increasing loss on Chinchilla-optimal models. Our law pairs a saturating benefit with a harm that grows logarithmically, reduces to Chinchilla without AI text, and predicts models 3.6 × \times larger than those it is fit on with lower error on human text than all eleven existing laws we test. It implies that training on unfiltered web text at August 2026’s AI share (31.1%) takes 1.6 × \times the compute of training on its human subset, rising to 3.0 × \times by 2028, that human text should be repeated before AI text is added, and that validation loss should be reported on human and AI text separately. We release Wild AI , with its AI, topic, and format labels, code, and all 800 models.
blocks.zh: 狂野的AI文本现在占了被过滤的网络爬行量的四分之一以上,其份额也在上升. 超过800个预先训练过的模型,它只帮助数据匮乏的模型,增加了钦奇拉最佳模型的损失. 我们的法则将饱和的好处与一种伤害相配,这种伤害会增长对数,在没有AI文本的情况下降低到Chinchilla,并且预言模型3.6×xx时间比人类文本上的错误小于我们检验的所有11种现有法律。 这意味着在2026年8月的AI共享时间(31.1%)上, 我们发布Wild AI, 带有它的AI,话题, 和格式标签,代码, 和所有800模型。

blocks.en: We fit our law on models up to 268M parameters and test it up to 973M. Larger models memorize more of their training data ( Carlini et al., 2023 ) and can be hurt more by model-generated data ( Dohmatob et al., 2025 ) , so they may pick up the patterns of weaker LLMs more readily. They might instead learn AI and human text as related tasks that help each other, a turn the joint law of Shukor et al. (2025) can express. We measure next-token loss, and at our sizes AI text raises CORE scores ( Li et al., 2024 ) about as much as fresh human text does (§ G ), although all models are too small to have meaningful performance, and these are the tasks AI-generated text was meant to optimize. We study only pretraining, on English web text labeled by Pangram. Future work could (1) filter wild AI text, as MAI does ( The Microsoft AI Team, 2026 ) , and add targeted synthetic data, (2) find the domains in which AI text helps, (3) measure how the AI text already in pretraining corpora has affected the quality of current models, and, as agents read other models’ outputs, (4) train models that understand AI-written input without writing like it, for example by tagging AI text ( Caswell et al., 2019 ) or masking its loss ( Lin et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 我们的模型定律达到268M参数 测试到973M 较大的模型会更多地记住他们的训练数据(Carlini等人,2023年),并且会因模型生成的数据(Dohmatob等人,2025年)而受到更多的伤害,因此它们可能更方便地拾取较弱的LLM的图案. 相反,他们可能学习人工智能和人文文本,作为互相帮助的相关任务,转而学习Shukor等人的共同法律。 (2025)可以表达. 我们测量下接的丢失,以我们的大小,AI文本提高了CORE的分数(Li等人,2024年),大约与人类新文本一样多(§G),虽然所有模型都太小,无法有有意义的性能,而这些都是AI生成的文本是为了优化的任务. 我们只研究预训, 在英文网页上, 未来的工作可以(1)过滤野生AI文本,如MAI所做的(微软AI Team,2026),并添加有针对性的合成数据,(2)找出AI文本帮助的领域,(3)衡量已经在预训中存在的AI文本如何影响当前模型的质量,当代理阅读其他模型的输出时,(4)理解AI书面输入的列车模型,而不像其写作,例如标记AI文本(Caswell等人,2019年)或掩盖其损失(Lin等人,2024年).

blocks.zh: 可复制声明

blocks.en: Data. Wild AI is FineWeb v1.4.0 extended to June 2026 by rerunning the FineWeb pipeline on Common Crawl (§ 2 , § A ); every document carries its EditLens and Pangram 3.3.2 provenance labels and WebOrganizer topic and format labels. We release all 83B tokens of Wild AI with these document-level labels.

blocks.en: Appendix A Data
blocks.zh: 附录A 数据

blocks.en: Wild AI combines two samples of English web text. The first is drawn from the 16 released FineWeb dumps, CC-MAIN-2024-10 to CC-MAIN-2025-26 ( Penedo et al., 2024a ) . The second extends FineWeb to the twelve Common Crawl dumps from July 2025 to June 2026 (CC-MAIN-2025-30 to CC-MAIN-2026-25): we rerun FineWeb’s DataTrove pipeline ( Penedo et al., 2024b ) on the first 2.6% of each dump’s WARC files, keeping 5.9M documents (4.6B tokens). In total, Wild AI has 96.04M documents and 83.31B tokens.
blocks.zh: Wild AI结合了英文网页文本的两个样本. 第一部取材自16家发布的FineWeb垃圾堆,CC-MAIN-2024-10至CC-MAIN-2025-26(Penedo等人,2024a). 第二次将FineWeb延伸至2025年7月至2026年6月的12个常见爬行垃圾堆(CC-MAIN-2025-30至CC-MAIN-2026-25):我们在每个垃圾堆的WARC文档中, Wild AI总共拥有96.04M文档和83.31B令牌.

blocks.en: EditLens (Llama-3.2-3B) first sorts documents into four buckets from human-written to AI-generated, averaging over up to three evenly spaced 512-token windows. We take its most human bucket as human candidates and its two most AI buckets as AI candidates, dropping the bucket between them. Pangram then labels every candidate: we run the Pangram 3.3.2 model on up to three disjoint 512-token windows per document (the first, middle and last) and call a document Human or AI only when every window agrees, and Mixed otherwise. On 2,000 documents from June 2026, these labels match those of the Pangram 3.3.2 API on 96.7%; only 4 documents flip between Human and AI (the others involve mixed). The filter audit of § A.1 is labeled the same way. We use the Pangram label to make the training pool, comprising 58.91M human documents (42.19B tokens) and 32.54M AI documents (35.32B tokens), with the 4.59M Mixed documents left out. FW26 holds the Human- and AI-labeled documents of a random sample of our January to June 2026 extension: its Mixed documents (7% of its tokens) are left out, and 22.3% is the AI share of the remaining tokens (20.1% of the tokens scored, since the evaluation drops the part of a document beyond one 2,048-token sequence and AI documents are longer). The filtering experiments of § 5 train on our human and AI pools mixed at that share. The monthly AI shares of § 2 come from a separate sample of 5,000 documents drawn at random from each of the 62 crawl months between January 2021 and August 2026 and labeled through the Pangram 3.3.2 API, taken from FineWeb through June 2025 and from randomly drawn WARC files of each crawl after (§ A.2 ).
blocks.zh: 编辑Lens(Llama-3.2-3B)第一种文档,从人写到AI生成的4个桶,平均超过3个均匀间距512个托肯窗口. 我们把它最人类的桶作为人类候选人, 和它最AI的桶作为AI候选人, Pangram然后给每个候选者贴上标签:我们每个文档(第一,中,最后)运行最多三个脱节的512个托肯窗口上的Pangram 3.3.2模型,并且只有在每个窗口都同意时才能调用文档Human或AI,另外也可以调用Mixed. 在2026年6月的2000份文件上,这些标签与96.7%的Pangram 3.3.2 API的标签相匹配;只有4份文件在Human和AI之间翻转(其他涉及混合). §A.1的过滤审计被贴上同样的标签。 我们使用Pangram标签制作训练池,包括58.91M人文文件(42.19B令牌)和32.54MAI文件(35.32B令牌),其中4.59M. 混合文件被排除在外。 FW26持有我们2026年1月至6月扩展的随机抽样的人类和AI标记文件:其混合文件(其代号的7%)被忽略,其余代号的AI份额为22.3%(占记号的20.1%),因为评价将文件部分从一个2,048个音节的序列中掉下来,AI文件更长). 第5节火车在我们的人类和AI池的过滤试验 混合在这个份额。 §2的月度AI股票来自从2021年1月至2026年8月的62个爬行月中随机抽取的5,000份文件的单独样本,并通过Pagram 3.3.2 API标注,取自FineWeb至2025年6月,以及从FineWeb随机抽取的WARC文件在之后的每次爬行(§A.2).

blocks.en: Web text crawled before ChatGPT’s release in November 2022 ( OpenAI, 2022 ) should contain almost no AI text, so the share Pangram labels AI there bounds its false-positive rate on web documents. Of the 60,000 documents the monthly sample draws from 2021 (5,000 for each of the twelve calendar months spanned by the nine 2021 crawls), Pangram 3.3.2 labels 37 AI (0.062%, 95% interval 0.045 to 0.085%; 0.04% of tokens) and 25 Mixed, in line with its reported false-positive rate of 0.05%. Some of these documents may be genuinely machine-generated, since earlier language models already wrote web text, so the false-positive rate on web text is at most this.
blocks.zh: ChatGPT于2022年11月发布前(OpenAI, 2022年), 在6万份文件中,每月抽样来自2021年(2021年9次爬行跨越的12个日历月,每个月5,000份),Pangram 3.3.2标签为37 AI(0.062%,95%间隔为0.045至0.085%;0.04%的印记)和25 Mixed,与其报告的0.05%的虚假阳性率一致。 其中一些文件可能是真实的机器生成的,因为早期的语言模型已经写出了网络文本,所以网络文本上的假阳性率最多就是这个.

blocks.en: We find that the makeup of the web is changing over time. Product pages grow from 14 to 22% of tokens while personal blogs fall from 15 to 6%. In 2026, about half of tutorial and knowledge-article tokens are AI-labeled (51 and 49%), against 9% of news and 5% of personal-blog tokens, as shown in Figure 8 . In our training pool, which was assembled to supply AI text (about 34% AI documents, against 8 to 13% on the web in 2024 and 2025), knowledge articles (60% of documents), tutorials (59%) and listicles (53%) lead the formats, against about 6% for comment sections, audio transcripts and spam. Fashion and beauty, home and hobbies, games and finance (40 to 46%) lead the topics, and politics (12%) trails, as shown in Figure 7 .
blocks.zh: 我们发现网络的构成随着时间的变化而变化. 产品页面从14个指数增长到22%,而个人博客则从15个下降到6%。 如图8所示,2026年,大约一半的辅导信和知识文章信条是AI标签(51%和49%),而9%的新闻信条和5%的个人博客信条。 在我们的训练库中, 提供AI文本(大约34%的AI文档, 而在2024年和2025年网络上为8%至13%), 知识文章(60%的文档)、教程(59%)和列表(53%)主导格式, 如图7所示,时尚与美貌、家居与爱好、游戏与金融(40%至46%)为主题、政治(12%)线索。

blocks.en: Figure 7: Knowledge articles, tutorials and listicles are the most AI-labeled formats in nearly every topic. Share of documents Pangram 3.3.2 labels AI in each WebOrganizer topic and format of our training pool documents.
blocks.zh: 图7 知识文章,教程和列表是几乎所有主题中最贴有AI标签的格式. Pangram 3.3.2 文档在WebOrganizer的每个话题和格式中标注AI的共享度 。

blocks.en: Figure 8: The web shifts toward the formats and topics AI writes most. We plot January 2021 to August 2026, Pangram 3.3.2 and WebOrganizer labels by calendar quarter. Each format’s and topic’s share of web tokens and the share of each format’s and topic’s tokens labeled AI.
blocks.zh: 图 8:网络转向格式和话题 AI写得最多. 我们绘制了2021年1月至2026年8月的Pagram 3.3.2和按日历季度划分的WebOrganizer标签. 每个格式和主题在网络符号中的份额以及每个格式和主题符号中的份额都标注为AI.

blocks.en: A.1 Effects of Quality Filtering
blocks.zh: A.1 质量过滤的影响

blocks.en: To understand the effects of quality filtration systems on AI-generated text in relation to human text, we sample 10,000 documents from 2026 Common Crawl. We replicate the FineWeb and DCLM filtration processes, and trace the proportion of AI-generated text that passes through each step in relation to the proportion of human text that survives. The filtration process is depicted in Figure 9 . Each pipeline runs on its own extraction of a 10,000-document sample from the same 32 WARC files of CC-MAIN-2026-30: FineWeb’s on text extracted with Trafilatura, as FineWeb does, and DCLM’s on text extracted with Resiliparse, as DCLM does, so the two samples hold different numbers of documents per label.
blocks.zh: 为了了解质量过滤系统对人工智能生成的文本相对于人类文本的影响,我们从2026年的Common Crawl抽取了10,000份文件. 我们复制了 FineWeb 和 DCLM 过滤过程,并追踪人工智能生成的文本相对于人类文本存活比例通过每个步骤的比例. 图9说明了过滤过程。 每个输油管都从CC-MAIN-2026-30的32个WARC文件中提取出10,000个文件样本:FineWeb在与Trafilatura一起提取的文本上,如FineWeb所做的那样;DCLM在Resiliparse身上提取的文本上,如DCLM所做的那样,因此两个样本每个标签持有不同的文件数量.

blocks.en: Figure 9: DCLM’s quality classifier keeps AI-labeled documents far more often than human ones. Survival of a 10,000-document 2026 Common Crawl sample through each stage of the FineWeb (top) and DCLM (bottom) pipelines, split by Pangram 3.3.2 label.
blocks.zh: 图9:DCLM的质量分类器保存AI标签文件的次数远多于人类文件. 通过FineWeb(顶部)和DCLM(底部)输油管的每个阶段,由Pangram 3.3.2标签分拆出一个10000文档的常用攀爬样本存活下来.

blocks.en: FineWeb keeps 29.3% of AI-labeled documents (282 of 963) and 12.8% of human-labeled ones (1,104 of 8,649), 2.3 × \times as often (95% interval 2.1 to 2.6 × \times ). AI documents pass its English filter more often (45% against 33%), and among English documents its quality heuristics keep 64% of AI documents and 39% of human ones. DCLM keeps 14.5% of AI documents (84 of 578) and 1.5% of human ones (129 of 8,697), 9.8 × \times as often (7.5 to 12.7 × \times ). The gap opens at its learned classifier, which keeps 40% of the AI documents that reach it and 9.5% of the human ones. AI documents survive more often within the same format, so the gap is not only a matter of format mix: among English documents, DCLM keeps 53% of AI-labeled knowledge articles against 17% of human ones, and 49% of AI tutorials against 20%.
blocks.zh: FineWeb保存着29.3%的AI标签文件(282 of 963)和12.8%的人标签文件(8,649中的1,104),2.3x\时间一样频繁(95%的间隔2.1到2.6x\时间). AI文档更频繁地通过英语过滤器(45%对33%),在英语文档中,其质量heuristics保存着64%的AI文档和39%的人文文档. DCLM保存着14.5%的AI文件(578年的84份)和1.5%的人类文件(8 697年的129份),9.8 × 时常(7.5到12.7 × 时). 差距在它所学的分类器中打开,它保留了40%到达它的AI文档和9.5%的人类文档. AI文档在相同的格式中生存得更频繁,因此差距不仅仅是格式组合的问题:在英文文档中,DCLM保存了53%的AI标签知识文章,而人类的则保存了17%,49%的AI教程则保存了20%.

blocks.en: Most removed human-labeled documents fail the English filters or are extraction debris (93% of truncated pages, 88% of content listings and 85% of structured data are removed after FineWeb’s English filter), but DCLM’s learned classifier also removes most human prose that reaches it, including 111 of 117 news articles and 106 of 117 personal blogs.
blocks.zh: 大多数被移除的人标注的文档都未能通过英语过滤器或者是提取碎片(在FineWeb的英语过滤器之后,93%的截断页,88%的内容列表和85%的结构化数据被移除),但DCLM的学习分类器也移除了大多数到达它的人标语,包括117篇新闻文章中的111篇和117篇个人博客中的106篇.

blocks.en: A.2 Forecasting the AI Share of the Web
blocks.zh: A.2 预测互联网的AI份额

blocks.en: Every month of the series covers its whole crawl. Up to June 2025 the 5,000 documents come from FineWeb, whose dumps span every WARC file of a crawl and which we read in a seeded random shard order. From July 2025 on, they come from 32 WARC files drawn at random from each crawl and run through the FineWeb filters. To forecast our future rates of AI, we take a sample of 10,000 documents from July and August 2026, past our data cutoff dates, as an evaluation sample. We find the rate of AI tokens in the samples was 27.9% for July and 31.1% for August. We compare several forecasting methods on held-out months, including ones that respect the bounds of a share (the lowest proportion of the web AI tokens can hold is 0, and the highest 100). We try ARIMA ( Box and Jenkins, 1970 ) , random walks with drift ( Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, 2021 ) , ordinary damped Holt ( Gardner and McKenzie, 1985 ) , and logit-damped methods (a damped trend on the logit of the share; Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, 2021 ) and choose a random walk with drift because it gave the most accurate predictions on months since ChatGPT ( OpenAI, 2022 ) was introduced in late November 2022. The July and August samples come from crawls after our June 2026 data cutoff (CC-MAIN-2026-30 and CC-MAIN-2026-34). They first served as a check on forecasts fit through June; the final forecasts refit the chosen random walk with drift through August 2026. We estimate 50.7% of text will be AI by the end of 2028, shown in Figure 10 and Table 2 .
blocks.zh: 系列的每个月都覆盖其整个爬行. 直至2025年6月,5000份文件都来自FineWeb,其垃圾堆遍及每个WAC文件的爬行,我们以种子随机硬度顺序阅读. 从2025年7月开始,它们来自32个WARC文件,从每个爬行中随机抽取,并运行在FineWeb过滤器中. 为了预测我们未来AI的速率,我们从2026年7月和8月,在数据截止日期之后,抽取了10,000份文件作为评价样本. 我们在样本中发现,7月的AI标志率为27.9%,8月为31.1%。 我们比较了被搁置月份的几种预测方法,包括尊重份额界限的方法(网络AI标志可持有的最小比例为0,最高的100)。 我们尝试了ARIMA(Box and Jenkins,1970年),随漂流的随机行走(Hyndman and Athanasopoulos,2021年),普通的拦坝霍尔特(Gardner and McKenzie,1985年),以及logit-damped方法(在股权的日志上被拦坝的趋势;Hyndman and Athanasopoulos,2021年),并选择随漂流的随机行走,因为它给出了自ChatGPT(OpenAI,2022年)于2022年11月下旬推出以来数月的最准确的预测. 7月和8月的样本来自我们2026年6月的数据截断(CC-MAIN-2026-30和CC-MAIN-2026-34)之后的爬行. 他们首先检查到6月份的预测;最后的预测对2026年8月之前选择的随漂移的随机行走进行重新评价。 我们估计,到2028年底,50.7%的文本将是大赦国际,如图10和表2所示。

blocks.en: Appendix B Training Configurations
blocks.zh: 附录B 培训配置

blocks.en: We report architecture details in Table 3 . All 800 models share one nanochat training recipe ( Karpathy, 2025 ) . The input embedding and output head are untied. N N counts the input embedding but not nanochat’s value-embedding tables, which are also lookups (16.8M parameters at 19.9M, 709M at 973M). The tokenizer is nanochat’s BPE with 32,768 tokens, and sequences hold 2,048 tokens. Muon ( Jordan et al., 2024 ) updates the transformer matrices (learning rate 0.02) and AdamW ( Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019 ) the embeddings, output head and scalars. The learning rate warms up over 40 steps, stays constant, and decays linearly over the last 65% of steps to 5% of its peak. A step holds 262,144 tokens at 19.9M and 35.8M, 524,288 from 86.2M to 268M, and 1,048,576 at 477M and 973M. The schedule spans all of a run’s tokens, so a run with added tokens trains for more steps than its control and decays later. Human and AI documents are interleaved in a fixed hashed order, and every AI or fresh-human addition trains on its control’s human documents, in the same order and with the same seed. 703 of the 800 runs use one seed; the other 97, all at 19.9M to 268M, are replicates with other seeds (46 cells trained with two, three or five seeds). Training uses bf16 with FP8 matrix multiplies on eight H100 GPUs. We score the final checkpoint in bits per byte on 15.7M tokens each of C4 and FW22, 12.1M of FW26, 9.6M of FW26-H, 2.2M of FW26-AI and 18.5M of Cosmopedia, each document scored at most once, and the validation split of Paloma’s 16 sources. Table 4 lists all 800 runs, and Table 5 shows the 365 in the matched-budget grid. The 38 filtering models of Figure 5 (left) and the six repetition models of § F.3 are not among the 800 and enter no fit.

blocks.en: Every law, ours and each comparator, is fitted on the same 726 models at the five development sizes (19.9M to 268M). The 74 models at 477M and 973M are held out. The human-only controls contribute their own residual, and every addition run (AI or fresh human) contributes the residual of its change in log loss against its own control, so that the fit is anchored on the paired contrasts of § 4 . Coefficients minimize a Huber loss on these residuals with bounded least squares, from a Chinchilla fit on the human-only runs as the starting point. blocks.en: We benchmark 11 other scaling laws, applying laws meant for repetition, data mixing, and surrogate data to see how AI-generated text most closely acts. The requirements each law meets and their performance on held-out runs are depicted in Figure 17 . Additional analyses benchmark laws on absolute loss instead of relative ( Table 10 ), on AI-generated target text ( Table 9 ), and on low ratios of AI-generated tokens ( Table 11 ). On Paloma, five comparators (Chinchilla, Muennighoff et al. , CD, ATLAS and Hamidieh et al. ) fit a data term that is negligible at the held-out token counts ( β \beta at its upper bound of 2.5, or for CD a credit window at its lower bound, R ⋆ < 0.003 R^{\star}<0.003 ). They predict no change from added AI text ( | Δ | ≤ 2.1 × 10 − 5 |\Delta|\leq 2.1\times 10^{-5} ), so all five score the error of predicting zero change, 9.15 (7.75 at r < 1 r<1 ). Refitting Chinchilla with β \beta allowed up to 10 gives the same error. On absolute error the ranking changes: CD and ATLAS predict the loss of the human-text sets best (12.51 and 13.65 on C4, against 14.09 for ours, all × 10 − 3 \times 10^{-3} ), while ours is best on Paloma and on the AI-text sets ( Table 10 ). Because the paired errors are much smaller, absolute error mostly measures how well a law predicts the loss of the human-only models at the held-out sizes. blocks.en: E.2 Comparison with the Joint Law of Shukor et al. (2025)
blocks.zh: E.2 与Shukor等人联合法的比较(2025年)

blocks.en: The joint law of Shukor et al. (2025) is the strongest published scaling law for modeling the effects of AI text. It is second to ours on human text and best on mixed and AI text ( Table 1 , Table 9 ). It has no separate benefit and harm terms, and its fits imply that a model trained on AI text reaches a lower loss floor on human text than one trained on human text ( Figure 18 , right). Its projections beyond the trained sizes are also unstable: fitted through 135M or through 268M, it projects opposite effects of AI text at 8B ( Figure 18 , middle). We trained no 8B model, so these are projections for either law.

blocks.en: Benchmark accuracy and fit to human text come apart. At 20 T ​ P ​ P h TPP_{h} , adding at least as many tokens as the human corpus holds raises CORE by 1.6 points with AI text and by 1.9 points with fresh human text (23 and 6 runs), yet C4 loss moves in opposite directions: up 2.3% with AI text and down 3.0% with fresh human text. Models trained with AI text answer benchmark questions about as well, but they model human text less closely and write more like AI ( Table 13 ). CORE’s tasks reward knowledge that AI web text also carries, while loss on human text also measures how well a model matches the formats and style of human writing, where AI text differs most ( Figure 2 , left).
